ontology.title: SAREF: the Smart Applications REFerence ontology
ontology.description: The Smart Applications REFerence ontology (SAREF) is intended to enable interoperability between solutions from different providers and among various activity sectors in the Internet of Things (IoT), thus contributing to the development of the global digital market.

entities.label: accomplishes
entities.definition: Links a certain entity (e.g., a device) to the task it accomplishes.

entities.label: Actuation
entities.definition: A saref:Actuation is the act of carrying out a procedure to control the state of the world using an actuator. It links to an actuator to describe what made the actuation, and to the controlled feature, property, property of interest, state, or state of interest. Typically, its input is a property value or a state. An actuation of a state (OP saref:controls) should have a state as input (OP saref:hasInput). Respectively, an actuation of a property should have a property value as input.

entities.label: Actuator
entities.definition: A device designed to control one or more properties or states of one or more features of interest.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Definition of Actuator is simplified and grounded on saref:controls. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

entities.label: Appliance
entities.definition: A device designed to accomplish a particular task for occupant use. It consumes, produces, or stores, some commodity.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Definition of saref:Appliance is grounded on tasks and commodities.

entities.label: Command
entities.definition: The lowest-level directives a function exposes to some network. Commands can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:Command is independent of any device.

annotations.v: Observe property, control property, observe state, control state, invoke action, cancel action, turn on or off, change color, subscribe, publish, etc. are all commands.
V3.2.1: Simplified definition and axiomatization of saref:Command. Added examples.

entities.label: Command Execution
entities.definition: Describes the execution of a command. Typically, its inputs and outputs are human understandable and relate to some feature of interest, such as its state (e.g., s4abcd:On), or the value of its temperature (e.g., property value 21.0 °C).

entities.label: Command Of Interest
entities.definition: The lowest-level directives a device supports and exposes to some network. Commands can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. A saref:CommandOfInterest is a directives actually supported by a device and exposed to some network.

annotations.v: Like for commands, commands of interest may be described in terms of their input parameters, outputs, and which properties or states they target.

Commands of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, commands of interest are useful to specify the actual property of interest or state of interest that is expected as input parameter, output, or that will be targeted.
The corridor smart light switch supports a command of kind “turn on/off”, which controls the state of the outdoor light.
The smart fridge supports a command of kind “observe temperature”, which observes the temperature of the fridge.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:CommandOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

entities.label: Commodity
entities.definition: A marketable item which may be supplied without qualitative differentiation.

annotations.v: SAREF refers to energy commodities such as electricity, gas, coal and oil.

Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:Commodity, for example from the ISDA taxonomy of commodities, the Standard International Energy product Classification (SIEC), the IRENA Energy Taxonomy or Wikidata.
V4.1.1: Removed examples of commodity categories.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:Commodity is simplified.

entities.label: consists of
entities.definition: A relationship indicating a composite entity that consists of other entities (e.g., a temperature/humidity sensor that consists of a temperature sensor and a humidity sensor)

annotations.v: A feature kind (respectively a feature of interest) may consist of (OP saref:consistsOf) other feature kinds (respectively feature kinds or features of interest).
The OP saref:consistsOf can link a composite property, property of interest, or property value to its individual components.
V3.2.1: Add local restrictions on consistsOf on feature of interest

entities.label: consumes
entities.definition: Links a feature kind, feature of interest, or device, to the commodity it consumes

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:consumes, saref:isConsumedBy, saref:produces, saref:isProducedBy, saref:stores, saref:isStoredBy.

entities.label: controls
entities.definition: Links a device, function, command, or procedure execution, to the feature, property, or state, it controls.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced property saref:controls, as sub-property of saref:targets. and generalization of saref:controlsProperty.

entities.label: Device
entities.definition: A tangible object designed to accomplish a particular task. In order to accomplish this task, the device performs one or more functions. An instance of saref:Device represents one specific real world entity.

annotations.v: For example, a washing machine is designed to wash (task) and to accomplish this task it performs a start and stop function.

Examples of devices are a light switch, a temperature sensor, an energy meter, a water flow meter, and a laundry dryer. A laundry dryer is designed to dry laundry, and to accomplish this task it has a start/stop function.
V3.2.1: Most axioms on saref:Device were useless and have been deleted.
V3.2.1: definition of saref:Device clarifies it's a real world entity.
V3.2.1: saref:Device is explicitly a subclass of saref:FeatureOfInterest and s4syst:System.

entities.label: Device kinds
entities.definition: Device kinds allow to describe kinds of devices, with common properties and common states having the same value, targeting the same properties and states, common functions, and common services. Devices kinds may be used to describe models of devices in online catalogues.

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Introduced class saref:DeviceKind
V4.1.1: Use SKOS to organize generic classes in taxonomies.

entities.label: Feature kinds
entities.definition: Feature kinds allow to describe kinds of features of interest, with common properties having the same value, and common states being the same. An instance of saref:FeatureKind represents an archetype of real world entities, for example to populate product catalogs.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced class saref:FeatureKind
V3.2.1: Use SKOS to organize generic classes in taxonomies.

entities.label: Feature of interest
entities.definition: A feature of interest represents any real world entity from which a property or a state may be targeted, such as observed and controlled. An instance of saref:FeatureOfInterest represents one specific real world entity.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest is clarified, not only properties are measured, but properties and states can be observed and controlled.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest: Clarify it's a specific real world entity.
V3.2.1: Definition of saref:FeatureOfInterest: allValuesFrom axioms are unnecessary and have been deleted.

entities.label: Function
entities.definition: Logical groups of commands that devices support to accomplish their tasks. Function can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:Function can apply to different devices.

annotations.v: To accomplish the task of controlling the light, a smart light switch may have a function for turning on and off the light, and another to set the luminosity of the light.
To accomplish the task of sensing the temperature, a temperature sensor should have a sensing function.
To accomplish the task of washing clothes, a washing machine should have a function for washing.
V3.2.1: Simplified definition and axiomatization of saref:Function. Added examples.

entities.label: Function of Interest
entities.definition: Logical groups of commands that devices support to accomplish their tasks. Function can target (OP saref:targets and its sub-properties) features, properties, or states. An instance of saref:FunctionOfInterest is supported by exactly one device.

annotations.v: A function of interest is the function of (OP saref:isFunctionOfInterestOf) exactly one device.

Functions of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, functions of interest are useful to specify which command is actually exposed, and which actual property of interest or state of interest it targets.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:FunctionOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

entities.label: has applicable time
entities.definition: Links an entity (e.g., a profile) to an instant or interval or other compound temporal entity expressed using OWL Time, which bounds temporally the applicable context of that entity.

entities.label: has command
entities.definition: Links a function or function of interest and the command it supports.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Domain of saref:hasCommand is relaxed to saref:Function or saref:FunctionOfInterest.

entities.label: has command kind
entities.definition: links a command of interest to its kind, a command.

entities.label: has command of interest
entities.definition: Links a function of interest to one of its commands of interest.

entities.label: has device kind
entities.definition: Links a device to its kind, a device kind. Kinds of devices describe models of devices, with common properties and common states having the same value, targeting the same properties and states, common functions, and common services.

entities.label: has feature kind
entities.definition: links a feature of interest to its kind, a feature kind

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduce hasClassKind for Class is Feature, Device, Property, State, Function, Command.

entities.label: has function
entities.definition: Links a feature kind or a device to one of its functions.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Domain of saref:hasFunction is relaxed.

entities.label: has function kind
entities.definition: links a function of interest to its kind, a function

entities.label: has function of interest
entities.definition: Links a device to one of its functions of interest.

entities.label: has identifier
entities.definition: Links some entity to its identifier. Extensions of SAREF may define sub-properties such as s4abcd:hasUUID, s4abcd:hasGTIN12, etc.

entities.label: has input
entities.definition: Links a command, operation, or procedure execution, to its inputs.

annotations.v: Different complementary commands can be defined for controlling a light. Turn on or off the light based on a desired state, toggle the light status of a specific light, set the luminosity level with a transition time, set the default transition time, start comfort.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasInput and saref:hasOutput.

entities.label: has mandatory command
entities.definition: Links a function and one of its mandatory commands

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced mandatory and optional commands.

entities.label: has manufacturer
entities.definition: A relationship identifying the manufacturer of an entity (e.g., device). The value is expected to be a string or a string with language tag.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Defined domain of saref:hasManufacturer to union of feature kind and feature of interest.

entities.label: has model
entities.definition: A relationship identifying the model of an entity (e.g., device). The value is expected to be a string or a string with language tag.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Defined domain of saref:hasModel to union of feature kind and feature of interest.

entities.label: has operation
entities.definition: Links a service to one of its operations.

entities.label: has optional command
entities.definition: Links a function and one of its optional commands

entities.label: has output
entities.definition: Links a command or operation to its outputs.

annotations.v: Different complementary commands can be defined for observing a smart home. Observe the temperature once will output the indoor temperature property; observe status of the entry door will output an open/close state.

entities.label: has phenomenon time
entities.definition: Links a procedure execution to the time that the result applies. It may be an interval or an instant, or some other compound temporal entity expressed using OWL Time.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasPhenomenonTime as part of general will to make SAREF and SOSA/SSN converge.

entities.label: has profile
entities.definition: Links a device to its profile. Its inverse is saref:isProfileOf. The device should be linked to a certain commodity using OP saref:consumes, saref:produces, or saref:stores, and optionally to some property or state using OP saref:targets or its sub-properties.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Relaxed domain of saref:hasProfile to saref:FeatureKind or saref:Device

entities.label: has property
entities.definition: Links a feature kind or a feature of interest to one of its properties.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: applicability of saref:hasProperty is relaxed to also saref:FeatureKind

entities.label: has property kind
entities.definition: links a property of interest to its kind, a property.

entities.label: has property of interest
entities.definition: Links a feature of interest to one of its properties of interest.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasPropertyOfInterest and saref:isPropertyOfInterestOf. Cannot use saref:hasProperty due to the combination of cardinality restrictions and sub-property chain axioms makes the ontology exist the OWL 2 DL prodile.

entities.label: has property value
entities.definition: Links a feature kind, a feature of interest, or a property of interest, to a property value.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasPropertyValue.

entities.label: has result
entities.definition: Links a procedure execution (e.g., an observation) to its result (e.g., a property value).

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasResult as part of general will to make SAREF and SOSA/SSN converge.

entities.label: has result time
entities.definition: Links a procedure execution to the instant of time when the activity was completed, expressed as an xsd:dateTime literal.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasResultTime as part of general will to make SAREF and SOSA/SSN converge.

entities.label: has revision number
entities.definition: Links some entity (e.g., a device) to its revision number.

entities.label: has state
entities.definition: Links a feature kind or a feature of interest to one of its states.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Relaxed domain of saref:hasState.

entities.label: has state kind
entities.definition: links a state of interest to its kind, a state

entities.label: has state of interest
entities.definition: Links a feature of interest to one of its states of interest.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:hasStateOfInterest and saref:isStateOfInterestOf, parallel to saref:hasPropertyOfInterest and saref:isPropertyOfInterestOf.

entities.label: has state value
entities.definition: Links a feature kind, a feature of interest, or a state of interest, to a state value.

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Introduced saref:hasStateValue.

entities.label: has timestamp
entities.definition: Links a procedure execution or a profile to an instant.

annotations.v: When the execution time and the phenomenon time are the same time instants, then DP saref:hasTimestamp can be used to simply link a procedure execution to the time of these instants, expressed as an xsd:dateTime literal.
Applied on a profile, it describes the applicable instant of that profile
V3.2.1: Tried to clarify definition of saref:hasTimestamp. Still unclear.

entities.label: has value
entities.definition: Value of a property value expressed as an RDF literal. Note that, even if decimal values are expected, values could use other datatypes.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Clarified definition of saref:hasValue.

entities.label: has version
entities.definition: Links some entity (e.g., a device) to its version.

entities.label: is accomplished by
entities.definition: A relationship identifying an entity (e.g., a device) that can accomplish a task.

entities.label: is command of
entities.definition: Links a command and a function or function of interest that supports it.

entities.label: is command of interest of
entities.definition: Links a command of interest to the function of interest it is a command of.

entities.label: is consumed by
entities.definition: Links a commodity to the feature kind, feature of interest, or device, that consumes it

entities.label: is controlled by
entities.definition: Links a feature, property, or state, to the device, function, command, or procedure execution, that controls it.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced property saref:isControlledBy.

entities.label: is execution of
entities.definition: Links a command execution to the command or command of interest that was executed. Also liks an operation execution to the operation that was executed

entities.label: is function of
entities.definition: Links a function to the feature kind or device it is a function of.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:isFunctionOf.

entities.label: is function of interest of
entities.definition: Links a function of interest to the device it is a function of.

entities.label: is measured in
entities.definition: A relationship identifying the unit of measure used for a certain entity.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Relaxed domain of saref:isMeasuredIn so it can apply to saref:PropertyValue as well as saref:Measurement. The new range will be enforced in the next major revision of SAREF.

entities.label: is observed by
entities.definition: Links a feature, property, or state, to the device, function, command, or procedure execution, that observes it.

entities.label: is offered by
entities.definition: Links a service to the device that exposes it to a network

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Clarified definition of saref:isOfferedBy.

entities.label: is operation of
entities.definition: Links an operation to the service it belongs to.

entities.label: is produced by
entities.definition: Links a commodity to the feature kind, feature of interest, or device, that produces it

entities.label: is profile of
entities.definition: Links a profile to the device it describes. The device should be linked to a certain commodity using OP saref:consumes, saref:produces, or saref:stores, and optionally to some property or state using OP saref:targets or its sub-properties.

entities.label: is property of
entities.definition: Links a property to the feature kind or feature of interest it is a property of.

entities.label: is property of interest of
entities.definition: Links a property of interest to the feature of interest it is a property of.

entities.label: is state of
entities.definition: Links a state to the feature kind or feature of interest it is a state of.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:isStateOf.

entities.label: is state of interest of
entities.definition: Links a state of interest to the feature of interest it is a state of.

entities.label: is stored by
entities.definition: Links a commodity to the feature kind, feature of interest, or device, that stores it

entities.label: is target of
entities.definition: Links a feature, property, or state, to the device, function, command, or procedure execution, that targets it.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced property saref:isActedUponBy.
V4.1.1: Renamed property saref:isActedUponBy into saref:isTargetOf.

entities.label: is value of property
entities.definition: Links a property value to the property or property of interest it is a value of.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:isValueOfProperty.

entities.label: is value of state
entities.definition: Links a state value to the state or state of interest it is a value of.

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Introduced saref:isValueOfState.

entities.label: made by
entities.definition: Links a procedure execution to the entity (e.g., device) that made it.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduce saref:madeBy (resp. saref:madeExecution) as generalization of saref:measurementMadeBy (resp. saref:makesMeasurement).

entities.label: made execution
entities.definition: Links an entity (e.g., device) to the procedure execution it made.

entities.label: Meter
entities.definition: A device designed to observe and additionally do some computation and/or display one or more properties of one or more features of interest.

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Definition of Sensor and Meter are updated to better distinguish one from the other.
V3.2.1: Definition of Meter is simplified and grounded on saref:observes. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

entities.label: Observation
entities.definition: A saref:Observation is the act of carrying out a procedure to estimate or calculate a value of a property of a feature of interest, or a state of a feature of interest. It links to a sensor to describe what made the observation, and to the observed feature, property, property of interest, state, or state of interest. Typically, its result is a property value or a state. An observation of a state (OP saref:observes) should have a state as a result (OP saref:hasResult). Respectively, an observation of a property should have a property value as a result.

entities.label: observes
entities.definition: Links a device, function, command, or procedure execution, to the feature, property, or state, it observes.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced property saref:observes, as sub-property of saref:targets. and generalization of measures.

entities.label: offers
entities.definition: Links a device to a service it exposes to a network.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Clarified definition of saref:offers.

entities.label: Operation
entities.definition: A saref:Operation is the means of a service to communicate in a procedure-type manner over the network (i.e. transmit data to/from other devices). It is the –machine interpretable– exposure of a –human understandable– command to a network.

annotations.v: Typically, a device connected to a given network offers one service for each of its functions of interest, and each service has one operation per command of interest of the function of interest it represents.

An operation may be described in terms of its inputs and outputs using OP saref:hasInput and saref:hasOutput. Inputs and outputs of operations typically describe the expected schema or shape of network messages.
To turn on a light, send a CoAP PUT request with CBOR content 0xf5 (true)

In the set of operations exposed by a smart light bulb on a given network, one may be dedicated to turn on and off the light and expect a boolean as input. Another one may be dedicated to set the luminosity status and expect a target luminosity level (a byte) and a transition time (encoded on two bytes).

In the set of operations exposed by a smart washing machine on a given network, one may be dedicated to set the water temperature for the washing cycle, and expected as input a enumerated value. Another one may be dedicated to start, pause, or stop the washing cycle.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:Operation and associated properties from oneM2M base ontology.

entities.label: Operation Execution
entities.definition: Describes the execution of an operation in a network: the–machine interpretable–  description of a communication between devices over the network. Typically, its input and result are network messages, that conform to the input and output of the executed operation.

entities.label: Procedure Execution
entities.definition: Represents the act of carrying out a procedure.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:ProcedureExecution.

entities.label: produces
entities.definition: Links a feature kind, feature of interest, or device, to the commodity it produces

entities.label: Profile
entities.definition: A saref:Profile describes the money earned (negative values) or paied (positive values) for the use (production or consumption) of a commodity by a device in a certain context.

annotations.v: OP saref:hasProfile links a device to its profile. The device should be linked to a certain commodity using OP saref:consumes, saref:produces, or saref:stores, and optionally to some property or state using OP saref:targets or its sub-properties.

The applicable context of a profile can be bound temporally using DP saref:hasTimestamp or its subproperties defined by SAREF extensions, or OP saref:hasApplicableTime which links to instant or interval or other compound temporal entity expressed using OWL Time.
The applicable context can be restricted to when the property of a feature of interest has some value (OPs saref:whenPropertyValue)
The applicable context can be restricted to when a feature of interest has a certain state (OPs saref:whenState).
OP saref:hasPrice links a profile to the money earned (negative values) or paid (positive values) for the use (production or consumption) of the commodity by the device.
V3.2.1: Class saref:Profile has been re-specified, to take into account findings from SAREF4ENER V1.2.1.

entities.label: has price
entities.definition: Links a profile to the money earned (negative values) or paid (positive values) for the use (production or consumption) of the commodity by the device

entities.label: Property
entities.definition: Identifiable qualities of features of interest that can be target of devices, such as observed or controlled. A property can apply to different features of interest.

annotations.v: Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:Property.
Air temperature, pressure, luminance, etc. are all properties.

Until SAREF V3.1.1, there was an ambiguity between whether properties should be specific or generic to features of interest. This ambiguity has been solved in SAREF V3.2.1, and the new modeling will be enforced in the next major revision of SAREF.
V3.2.1: The definition and scope of usage for saref:Property is clarified. Axiomatization is simplified.

entities.label: Property of Interest
entities.definition: Identifiable qualities of features of interest that can be target of devices, such as observed or controlled. An instance of saref:PropertyOfInterest is specific to a feature of interest. It is inherent to and cannot exist without that feature of interest.

annotations.v: A property of interest is the property of (OP saref:isPropertyOfInterestOf) exactly one feature of interest.
Per convention, the IRI of properties of interest should consist of the IRI of their feature of interest, suffixed with a fragment identifier #{P} where {P} refers to the name of the property.

Properties of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, properties of interest are useful in applications, where the association between a feature of interest and a property (i.e., the property of interest) needs to be identified and related to other properties of interest.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:PropertyOfInterest to solved the ambiguity between generic vs specific properties.

entities.label: Property Value
entities.definition: Describes the value for a property. The property value is optionally linked to its value expressed as an RDF literal (DP saref:hasValue), optionally to the unit of measurement (OP saref:isMeasuredIn), and optionally to the properties or properties of interest it is a value of (OP saref:isValueOfProperty).

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Introduced saref:PropertyValue to simplify the association of a measure to a property, without always needing it to be a measurement made by a device.
V4.1.1: saref:hasValue is now optional on saref:PropertyValue.

entities.label: represents
entities.definition: Links a service to some function or function of interest it exposes to the network. Also links an operation to some command or command of interest it exposes to the network.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: Relaxed domain and range of saref:represents.

entities.label: Sensor
entities.definition: A device designed to observe and measure one or more properties or states of one or more features of interest.

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Definition of Sensor and Meter are updated to better distinguish one from the other.
V3.2.1: Definition of Sensor is simplified and grounded on saref:observes. Local restriction on saref:hasFunction is deleted.

entities.label: Service
entities.definition: A saref:Service is a digital representation of a function in a network, making it discoverable, registerable and remotely controllable in the network.

annotations.v: Typically, a device connected to a given network offers one service for each of its functions of interest.

For example, a light switch can offer the service of remotely switching the lights in a home through mobile phone devices that are connected to the local network (ex:SwitchOnService class). This "remote switching" service represents the ex:OnOffFunction.
V3.2.1: Simplified definition of saref:Service. Added examples.

entities.label: State
entities.definition: Identifiable conditions that features of interest are or may be in, and that can be target of devices, such as observed and controlled. A state can apply to different features of interest.

annotations.v: SAREF is not restricted to binary states such as the ex:OnOffState, but allows to define also enumerated states.
Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:State.
A switch can be found in the saref:OnOffState.
V3.2.1: Clarified and generalized definition of saref:State. Can now apply to all features of interest, not just devices.

entities.label: State of Interest
entities.definition: Identifiable conditions that features of interest are or may be in, and that can be target of devices, such as observed and controlled. An instance of saref:StateOfInterest is specific to a feature of interest. It is inherent to and cannot exist without that feature of interest.

annotations.v: A state of interest is the state of (OP saref:isStateOfInterestOf) exactly one feature of interest.
Per convention, the IRI of states of interest should consist of the IRI of their feature of interest, suffixed with a fragment identifier #{S} where {S} refers to the name of the state.

States of interest need not always be explicited. It depends on the use case. Typically, states of interest are useful in applications, where the association between a feature of interest and a state (i.e., the state of interest) needs to be identified and related to other states of interest.
V3.2.1: Introduced saref:StateOfInterest, parallel to saref:PropertyOfInterest.

entities.label: State Value
entities.definition: Describes the value for a state. The state value is optionally linked the states or states of interest it is a value of (OP saref:isValueOfState).

annotations.v: V4.1.1: Introduced saref:StateValue.

entities.label: stores
entities.definition: Links a feature kind, feature of interest, or device, to the commodity it stores

entities.label: targets
entities.definition: Links a device, function, command, or procedure execution, to the feature, property, or state, it targets.

annotations.v: V3.2.1: saref:actsUpon now holds not only between a command and a state. It generalizes observes, observes, controls. Domain and range are unions of several classes.
V4.1.1: saref:actsUpon is renamed saref:targets.

entities.label: Task
entities.definition: The goal for which a device is designed, from a user perspective.

annotations.v: Tasks can be accomplished by devices (saref:isAccomplishedBy).
For example, a washing machine is designed for the task of washing.

entities.label: Unit of measure
entities.definition: The unit of measure is a standard for measurement of a quantity, such as a Property.

annotations.v: Our definition is based on the definition of unit of measure in the Ontology of units of Measure (OM).
Concepts from existing code lists, vocabularies, and taxonomies, may be used as instances of saref:UnitOfMeasure. For example the QUDT Unit vocabulary

For example, consumption power is a property and Watt is a unit of power that represents a definite predetermined power: when we say 10 Watt, we actually mean 10 times the definite predetermined power "Watt".

entities.label: when property value
entities.definition: Links a profile to a property value that contributes to restricting its applicable context.

entities.label: when state
entities.definition: Links a profile to a state that contributes to restricting its applicable context.
